events.label: PLTR Q2 2026 earnings AH — $1.808B consensus (+81% YoY); government $916M is the DoD AI thesis validator
events.note: Updated Aug 3 morning: PLTR reports Q2 2026 AH tonight at 5 PM ET. Options pricing ~12% swing. Government revenue $916M (+65.7% YoY), commercial $892M (+98%), total $1.808B (+81%); Oppenheimer projects 85% growth vs. 79% company midpoint. Rate backdrop significantly eased: September hike now ~63% (down from 82.4% Friday) after Trump paused Iran strikes and restarted talks, sending Brent to $83.32 (cleared) and WTI to $79.54 (borderline). The valuation headwind is lighter, but PLTR at 130x trailing non-GAAP still requires a clean government revenue beat plus raised FY26 guidance above the 79% midpoint. A government revenue miss removes the DoD urgency premium regardless of the rate environment.

events.label: July NFP (BLS, 8:30 AM ET) — September rate path with hike odds at 63%; consensus +91K
events.note: Updated Aug 3 morning: September hike probability has dropped to ~63% (from 82.4% Friday) after Trump paused Iran strikes and oil collapsed. Consensus: +91K (prior 147K, unemployment 4.2%→4.3% expected). Above 150K: September hike rebounds above 70%, re-breaching the trigger; 30Y could extend back toward 5.28%. Below 80K: September probability falls toward 50% or below, beginning to clear the final formal rate-side breach (30Y) on a lagged basis. The NFP matters more than usual given the rapid oil-driven regime improvement on Aug 3 — a strong jobs print could restore 2 of the 2 breaches that just cleared. FOMC September 15-16.

events.label: AMD Q2 2026 earnings AH — MI300 GPU data-center traction vs. AMZN custom silicon ($25B+ ARR)
events.note: Added Aug 3 morning: AMD reports Q2 2026 AH Tuesday Aug 4 at 5 PM ET. Consensus: EPS $1.34 (+396% YoY). Data-center GPU revenue vs. MI300 adoption rate is the binary; AMZN custom silicon ($25B+ annual run rate) adds competitive read-through. PLTR Monday AH print sets the AI spending sentiment heading into AMD's call. Rate headwind eased modestly (September hike ~63% vs. 82.4% Friday) but AMD is −27.7% from June ATH on rate-driven multiple compression. Options pricing ~12.28% swing.

events.label: July CPI (est.) — Iran oil re-surge and tariff pass-through fully embedded
events.note: Updated July 30 night: July CPI embeds the Iran oil re-surge to $90.74 (Jul 29) and the bounce to ~$89.50 (Jul 30 on US retaliation) on top of the already-elevated July Brent average. Trump tariffs on 99.4% of imports remain a second CPI input. Even with today's soft June Core PCE (+0.1% MoM), July CPI is likely to show oil-driven re-acceleration. A print above 3.5% makes September hike near-certain regardless of ECI or Jackson Hole framing. Bull scenario (CPI ≤2.8%): ceasefire restores, oil retreats, soft PCE extends. Bear scenario (CPI ≥3.8%): oil + tariff dual pass-through; September 50bps probability escalates.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — AWS 37% + Azure 43% are the strongest pre-earnings demand confirmations
events.note: Updated July 30 night: AMZN AWS 37% (fastest in 18 quarters; AI + chips each >$25B annual run rate, triple-digit growth) alongside MSFT Azure 43% provides the strongest dual-confirmation of organic AI compute demand the series has seen entering an NVDA call. If enterprise customers funding AWS and Azure at these growth rates are paying from their own capital (not NVDA-backstopped), the circular financing concern is structurally reduced. On the Q2 FY27 call: (1) Circular financing disclosure — OpenAI $250B backstop still unaddressed; (2) AWS/Azure growth implies NVDA demand is real; (3) AMD MI400 share capture in hyperscaler buildout remains the key competitive question; (4) Kimi K3 efficiency headwind unchanged; (5) CXMT Chinese DRAM competition unchanged. Hard stop $216 intact.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote on September FOMC path
events.note: Updated July 31 night: Q2 ECI printed +0.9% QoQ (in-line), but September hike probability surged to 82.4% — above the 70% formal trigger — because the bond market treated in-line as insufficient dovish relief given Brent ~$91/bbl and the FOMC's 9-3 dissent structure. Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29) is now the most consequential Fed communication between today and the September 15-16 FOMC decision. With September already at 82.4%, the Warsh keynote will function as a de-facto September rate preview: any 'live meeting' framing locks September; any de-escalation framing (data dependence, growth risk) could push September back below 70%. July NFP (Aug 7) and July CPI (Aug 13) are the two data inputs that arrive before Jackson Hole and determine the probability range Warsh must address.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. Re-entry gate $115–120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors. Net losses structural ($4.9B in 2025). December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Watch Starlink ARR growth and Starship launch cadence as primary metrics.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off −13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst. Note: NVDA's circular financing story ($250B OpenAI backstop; July 27–28 WSJ/Bloomberg) adds complexity to the OpenAI IPO timeline if the guarantee structure is disclosed in S-1 filings. MSFT Azure 43% Q4 FY26 and AMZN AWS 37% Q2 both strengthen the narrative that OpenAI's compute investments have downstream demand — relevant for S-1 framing.
